ingredients.item: beef short ribs, flanken-cut across the bone, 8–10 mm thick
ingredients.preparation: 6–8 pieces; order "LA galbi cut" at a Korean market

ingredients.item: scallions , sliced; 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Steamed rice , lettuce and perilla leaves for ssam, ssamjang , pajeori , kimchi , garlic cloves sliced thick

instructions.heading: Set the fire for medium-hot, two-zone if you can
instructions.action: Set the fire for medium-hot, two-zone if you can. Charcoal burned down to gray-edged coals, or a grill you can hold your hand over for 3–4 seconds at the cooking height (around 200 °C). Galbi's sugar wants to blacken; a cooler zone gives you an escape hatch when a strip lacquers before the meat at the bone is done. Lay the strips in one layer, bone side down first.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the first minute tells you if the fire is right: steady sizzle, light smoke, the smell of caramelizing soy. Violent flare-ups mean drip fat found the coals — move the strip, don't lose it.

instructions.heading: Grill 3–4 minutes a side, flipping once or twice
instructions.action: Grill 3–4 minutes a side, flipping once or twice. The grill boss's law: leave the strips alone until the edges weep and the underside goes mahogany, then flip with tongs — never a fork; the juice is the point. The second side takes a minute less. If a strip's sugars run ahead of the meat, shift it to the cool zone and close the lid for 90 seconds; steam finishes the center while the lacquer rests.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the pull test: the meat between the bones has firmed, the surface is glossy mahogany with char in the crosshatch scores, and the cut edge at a bone shows no raw red — a sliver of pink at the bone is right, raw is not. One test piece eaten at the grill boss's station is traditional and non-negotiable.

instructions.heading: Scissors, platter, ssam
instructions.action: Scissors, platter, ssam. Pull the strips and cut them with kitchen scissors into single-bone pieces, straight onto a warm platter at the table's center. Sesame and scallion over; the pieces go straight into waiting ssam: leaf, a thin swipe of ssamjang (#SA01), a piece of galbi while it is still hot, a strand of pajeori or a slice of raw garlic, fold, one bite. The bone gets gnawed at the table; that is what bones are for.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the ssam test: one bite, everything at once — sweet lacquer edge, juicy beef, ssamjang's fermented depth, the leaf's snap. If the galbi overpowers the ssamjang, the marinade ran sweet; trim the sugar next batch by a fifth. If the ssam falls apart, less is in the leaf than you think is enough.

visualDonenessCues: The cut: flanken, 8–10 mm, crosshatch scored, membrane off.
The marinade: blended smooth, 6–24 hours, flat single layer.
The grill: mahogany lacquer, char in the scores, no raw red at the bone, a sliver of pink allowed.
The table: scissors to single bones, ssam while hot, bones gnawed.
storageNotes: Marinated strips keep 24 hours (freeze in the marinade up to a month, thaw overnight — the pear keeps working, so freeze flat and early). Cooked galbi keeps 3 days; chop and fry into kimchi fried rice with the bones for stock.

Variations: the garlic-sesame boneless galbisal (#M05) is the same joint's quieter cousin; the gochujang lacquer fork (#M04) for the spice-first table; braised galbijjim is another record's road entirely — do not braise this cut into it.
